name: season_forecast
label: If the show had kept going
description: Season 13 (2025) and Season 14 (2026), each with everyday mishaps only and if a catastrophe hits (has_forecast_catastrophe, the page's filter): expected cost with its 80% range, expected mishaps, everyday losses by kind and the chance of a catastrophe, in dollars of the year it airs.

metrics.name: forecast_loss_median
metrics.label: Expected Cost
metrics.description: The season's median simulated total loss: everyday mishaps only, or plus a catastrophe when grouped by has_forecast_catastrophe = 1. Half the simulated seasons cost less, half more. In dollars of the year it airs.

metrics.name: forecast_loss_p10
metrics.label: Low End
metrics.description: 10th percentile of the season's simulated total loss: 1 in 10 simulated seasons cost less. With the high end, the 80% range.

metrics.name: forecast_loss_p90
metrics.label: High End
metrics.description: 90th percentile of the season's simulated total loss: 1 in 10 simulated seasons cost more. With the low end, the 80% range.

metrics.name: forecast_mishaps_median
metrics.label: Expected Mishaps
metrics.description: The season's median simulated number of everyday mishaps.

metrics.name: forecast_mishaps_p10
metrics.label: Mishaps (low end)
metrics.description: 10th percentile of the season's simulated everyday mishap count.

metrics.name: forecast_mishaps_p90
metrics.label: Mishaps (high end)
metrics.description: 90th percentile of the season's simulated everyday mishap count.

metrics.name: forecast_realized_loss_median
metrics.label: Everyday Realized
metrics.description: Median simulated total of the season's everyday realized losses (money or property actually lost). Not part of a sum: the medians of the pieces don't add up to the median of the whole.

metrics.name: forecast_hypothetical_loss_median
metrics.label: Everyday Hypothetical
metrics.description: Median simulated total of the season's everyday hypothetical losses (missed income). Most simulated seasons have one or none, so the median is small; a big missed opportunity shows up in the high end instead.

metrics.name: forecast_catastrophe_chance
metrics.label: Chance of a Catastrophe
metrics.description: Chance the season has a catastrophe that could happen again (the house fire or Latte Larry's): the share of the 12 real seasons that had one. The divorce is left out: it was the show's one divorce, and Larry ends the series unmarried.

metrics.name: forecast_episodes
metrics.label: Forecast Episodes
metrics.description: Episodes in the forecast season (10, like every real season).
